chapter_title: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
core_summary: Everyday transformations are classified into physical and chemical changes. A physical change alters physical properties (shape, size, phase, appearance) without altering chemical composition or forming new substances (e.g., melting ice, tearing paper, dissolving sugar). Physical changes are usually reversible. A chemical change (chemical reaction) converts one or more substances into entirely new chemical substances with distinct properties (e.g., rusting iron, burning magnesium, curdling milk, composting organic waste). Chemical changes are generally irreversible.
key_concepts: To classify vegetable prep and composting activities as physical or chemical changes.

key_terms.definition: A change in which a material undergoes alteration in physical form without creating any chemically new substance.
A process where chemical bonds are broken and formed, yielding one or more distinct new substances.

key_takeaways: Some physical changes are irreversible, such as tearing paper or breaking glass, even though no new chemical substance is created.
